practices.practice: Create one MongoClient per process and reuse it (module/global singleton) rather than creating a new client per request.
Read the cluster connection string only from environment variables (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never hard-code or write it to logs or files.
practices.prior_belief: Read the cluster connection string (Mongo URI) only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never hard-code or commit it, and never write it to logs or files.

practices.practice: Always use TLS for connections and do not disable certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Enable TLS in the Mongo client (tls=true / ssl=true) and require certificate validation; do not connect with insecure TLS settings.

practices.practice: Tune connection-pool and driver timeouts to your deployment pattern (serverless: small pools, short maxIdleTimeMS; long-running servers: larger pools and longer idle times); set serverSelectionTimeoutMS/connectTimeoutMS/socketTimeoutMS appropriately.
practices.prior_belief: Use connection pooling and set sensible driver options (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) appropriate for concurrent multi-agent workload; tune pools to match number of agent worker threads/processes.

practices.practice: Implement retry semantics for transient errors and throttling: use exponential backoff with jitter, honor 429 / Retry-After responses where applicable, and prefer driver-provided retryReads/retryWrites combined with application retries for idempotent operations.
practices.prior_belief: Implement robust retry semantics for transient errors and throttling: exponential backoff, jitter, idempotent-safe retries, and respect 429/Retry-After headers returned by the service.

practices.practice: Prefer Microsoft Entra ID / managed identity + RBAC for application authentication and avoid embedding primary keys in application code; create least-privilege secondary users if you must use SCRAM credentials and store secrets in a secret manager (Key Vault).
practices.prior_belief: Secure credentials using Azure Key Vault or equivalent secret manager; do not place primary keys in source control or test fixtures; use environment-specific config placeholders (.env.example) for onboarding.

practices.practice: Restrict network access using Private Endpoints and firewall rules; disable public network access for production clusters where possible.
practices.prior_belief: Use private network access controls (IP firewall rules, VNet/private endpoint) to limit database access to your CI/dev machine and build environment rather than leaving the cluster open to the internet.

practices.practice: Use explain('executionStats') (or the MCP explain_operation tool) on finds and aggregation pipelines to verify index usage, check for COLLSCAN vs IXSCAN, and measure keysExamined/docsExamined before and after index changes.
practices.prior_belief: Use explain() or the MCP server tools to inspect aggregation query plans when tuning pipelines or indexes; check whether stage is COLLSCAN vs IXSCAN and iterate on index design accordingly.

practices.practice: Create indexes that match the fields used in filters and early $match stages; prefer a well-ordered compound index following the ESR (Equality → Sort → Range) rule rather than many single-field indexes and verify with explain.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes for the exact fields used in filters and the early $match stages of aggregation pipelines (compound indexes when queries filter on multiple fields); verify with explain() that the index is used.

practices.practice: Keep a modest index budget (review $indexStats), drop or hide unused indexes safely (hide → drop lifecycle) and avoid creating many overlapping single-field indexes.

For vector search, store embeddings with the exact embedding dimensionality and create a vector index with matching dimensions and similarity; mismatched dimensions/similarity produce silently incorrect results and you must rebuild the index if you change the model.
practices.prior_belief: For vector search, store embeddings as a single array field with fixed dimensionality and create the vector index (HNSW/IVF) with the matching dimension and chosen metric (cosine/innerProduct/Euclidean) before running similarity queries.

practices.practice: Pick the vector index engine to match scale (prefer DiskANN for production at scale, HNSW for mid-scale, IVF for small collections) and tune index/query parameters (maxDegree, lBuild, lSearch) to trade off recall vs latency.

When running aggregation pipelines, push $match and $project stages as early as possible, use allowDiskUse for large groups or sorts, and verify the plan with explain() to avoid COLLSCANs and blocking in-memory sorts.
practices.prior_belief: When running heavy aggregation pipelines, push $match and $project stages as early as possible to reduce working set, use allowDiskUse when needed for large groups/sorts, and monitor RU consumption for the pipeline.

practices.practice: Make seed scripts idempotent by using upsert/replaceOne (or per-document upserts); do not assume server-side bulkWrite is available — check the compatibility table because bulkWrite is not supported in some Azure DocumentDB Mongo compatibility versions.
practices.prior_belief: Seed collections using bulkWrite/bulk insert with unordered operations for speed; handle duplicate-key errors gracefully and make seed scripts idempotent by upserting on unique keys.

practices.practice: Include a schemaVersion (or schemaVersion) field in persisted documents and perform lazy per-document migration so older documents remain readable as the application evolves.
practices.prior_belief: Include a schema_version field on persisted documents and migrate readers (or write migration code) so stored stress_run documents remain readable as the app evolves.

practices.practice: Keep documents well under the 16 MB BSON document limit; split very large binary blobs or long histories into separate storage (blob storage) and reference them from documents.
practices.prior_belief: Limit document size to avoid service document size limits (keep documents small—store large binary blobs or long histories in separate storage like blob storage and reference them), and design audits to avoid exceeding the database item size cap.

practices.practice: Monitor cluster metrics (CPU %, memory/working set, IOPS, storage used, connection count, failed connections), enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs, and alert on saturation signals appropriate to your cluster tier.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor RU/s, request charge per query, index usage, latency, and throttling metrics in Azure Monitor and instrument the app to log RU costs returned by the server for expensive aggregation runs.

practices.practice: Pick a shard/partition key aligned with your query patterns and cardinality goals (read-heavy → choose frequent query filter; write-heavy → choose high-cardinality field); plan partitioning/shard key up front because changing it later is costly.
practices.prior_belief: Choose a partition key that aligns with query patterns and evenly distributes load (e.g., account_id or tenant_id), and create collections with partitioning configured up front rather than trying to repartition later.

practices.practice: Guard against hot partitions by avoiding very low-cardinality keys and by designing queries to include the partition key where possible; monitor uneven CPU/IOPS/storage across shards and reshard if necessary.
practices.prior_belief: Guard against hot partitions and skewed RU consumption by avoiding very low-cardinality partition keys (e.g., a single constant value) and by designing queries to include the partition key where possible.

practices.practice: For new clusters prefer Premium SSD v2 storage (default recommendation) and size compute tier for throughput (IOPS/bandwidth) rather than increasing disk size for IOPS.
When developing locally, use the DocumentDB Gateway image (Mongo protocol on port 10260) and drive TLS relaxation from environment variables; do not default tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=true in code.
Azure DocumentDB supports multi-document ACID transactions; consult the product docs for constraints (compatibility/version notes) before avoiding transactions wholesale.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid multi-document transactions where possible; design updates to be single-document atomic (use $inc/$set) or use application-level compensation, because distributed transactions are limited/expensive on managed DocumentDB/Mongo APIs.
practices.source_name: Group multiple operations in transactions in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Prefer Entra/managed-identity authentication for production apps and create least-privilege secondary users if SCRAM credentials are necessary; rotate secondary-user passwords regularly.
When changing embedding models, rebuild the vector index (dimensions and similarity must match); store the embedding model name and dimensionality alongside vectors to avoid silent mismatches.
Use diagnostic settings to emit slow-query logs to Log Analytics and combine metric alerts (CPU/memory/IOPS/connections) with slow-query signals for actionable alerting.
Create useful indexes (instrument, account_id, currency, nested fields) as part of seed/index scripts so sample data and queries run efficiently and idempotently.

If a driver or command isn't supported on Azure DocumentDB (check the compatibility table), adapt code to supported alternatives rather than assuming Mongo server parity (e.g., use replaceOne upsert loops when bulkWrite is not supported).
practices.source_name: MongoDB Query Language (MQL) compatibility in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Do not assume Cosmos DB-specific metrics (RUs/request-charge) apply; Azure DocumentDB uses compute + storage billing and exposes direct cluster metrics (CPU, memory, IOPS) instead.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor RU/s, request charge per query, index usage, latency, and throttling metrics in Azure Monitor and instrument the app to log RU costs returned by the server for expensive aggregation runs.

practices.practice: When diagnosing performance, use the MCP tools or mongosh commands to list indexes, sample documents, get collection stats, and run explain() for the aggregation pipeline before changing indexes.

If a recommended audit document shape is desired (immutable, run_id, created_at, schema_version, scenario_parameters, agent_outputs, aggregated_results, provenance), treat that as an application-level convention — the public Azure DocumentDB docs recommend schemaVersion but do not prescribe a canonical stress-test run document shape.
practices.prior_belief: Store each stress-test run as an immutable audit document with fields: run_id, created_at (ISO8601), schema_version, scenario_parameters, agent_outputs (raw), aggregated_results, run_status, and provenance (user/service), so runs are auditable and replayable.

practices.practice: There is no public guidance that Azure DocumentDB prefers a specific client-level consistency (e.g., Session) for general application throughput; consistency guidance visible in Azure docs is tied to Cosmos DB, not the Azure DocumentDB managed Mongo-compatible service.
practices.prior_belief: Prefer Session consistency (or the appropriate lower-latency consistency) for application throughput, and only opt for strong consistency when strictly required by correctness/audit semantics.

practices.practice: For unit and integration testing, Azure guidance focuses on local gateway images and environment-driven config for integration tests; there is no single Azure DocumentDB doc prescribing test mocking patterns — use lightweight mocks or an isolated live test database as appropriate to your test strategy.
practices.prior_belief: In unit tests prefer lightweight mocks for DB calls or run integration tests against an isolated live test database; avoid mocking patterns that create a new MagicMock on every __getitem__ (which breaks dictionary-style access) — return a stable fake document or use mongomock/mini cluster.
practices.how_found: Searched: 'Azure DocumentDB testing mongomock', 'unit tests DocumentDB mock patterns', 'DocumentDB integration tests local gateway' and reviewed local-deployment guidance (gateway image) but found no single Azure-prescribed unit-test mocking style
